clean_body: This work reflects what I believe the government should do: deliver practical results and make life better for the people it serves. | | | | Since the start of the year, I have been working to protect jobs, strengthen infrastructure, help communities recover from recent flooding, and push for greater transparency and accountability in government. I want to share a few of the ways I have been working to deliver results since January: 1\. Addressing Affordability, Lowering Costs, and Protecting the Regional Economy What people in Northwest Washington are facing: Higher prices tied to tariffs and economic instability Dependence on major regional employers (especially aerospace) Supply chain and trade disruptions that affect workers and businesses What I am doing: Supporting efforts to end tariffs that raise costs for consumers and businesses, and increasing prices on groceries, energy, and health care. Advocating for job growth in aerospace, including the upcoming Boeing production expansion that creates jobs for regional workers. Passing federal funding packages that invest in jobs, education, and infrastructure. 2\. Infrastructure, Transportation, and Local Project Funding What people in Northwest Washington are facing: Aging transportation infrastructure Need for transit and port investments Regional economic growth tied to mobility and logistics What I am doing: Securing federal infrastructure funding for projects across Northwest Washington. Opening applications for Community Project Funding that directs federal dollars to local governments and nonprofits. Bringing money home to Northwest Washington to support investments that strengthen infrastructure, community facilities, and economic development. 3\. Disaster Recovery and Climate Resilience What people in Northwest Washington are facing: Recent flooding has made disaster recovery and climate resilience an immediate concern. Damaged infrastructure, homes, and businesses. Increasing frequency and severity of climate-related disasters. What I am doing: Supporting federal disaster assistance and pushing for a major disaster declaration to repair damaged infrastructure. Connecting communities with resources like the new SBA loans to help businesses rebuild after floods. Raising the alarm about the real-world impacts of climate change on Northwest Washington communities. 4\. Public Safety and the Opioid Crisis What people in Northwest Washington are facing: The opioid epidemic continues to affect communities across Northwest Washington Need for treatment, prevention, and law enforcement resources What I am doing: Securing federal funding for addiction recovery programs, public safety initiatives, and law enforcement efforts to disrupt trafficking. Framing the opioid crisis as a community-wide challenge requiring federal support and coordination. 5\. Accountability, Democracy, Oversight, and Supporting Our Servicepeople What people in Northwest Washington are facing: Impacts of dark money in elections A reckless approach to immigration enforcement An undermining of Congressional authority on war powers What I am doing: Reintroducing the DISCLOSE Act to end dark money in elections and increase transparency in political spending. Opposing DHS funding proposals that lack accountability for ICE enforcement actions. Voting to require congressional authorization for military hostilities involving Iran. Supporting Coast Guard investments and maritime safety infrastructure. Launching community initiatives recognizing veterans and servicemembers. All of this work reflects what I believe government should do: deliver practical results and make life better for the people it serves. But continuing that work will require building a strong campaign this election year. Republicans are already preparing to defend their House majority. Taking back the House is critical to restoring stability in Washington and making progress on the issues that matter most to Northwest Washington. = = Preparing for the next election starts early. With your help, we can continue building a campaign that stands up for the values of Northwest Washington and works to deliver real results for our communities. Hi friends , it’s been a few months since California voters overwhelmingly passed Prop 50 and established updated congressional districts to counter Trump’s midterm power grab.
I want to take a second to talk about what winning in these new maps looks like, and what you can do to help.
First, let’s talk CA-51:
My district was actually made a bit more competitive in the new maps, by about 4-5 points.
It was stretched to the east, absorbing areas previously in the 48th District (represented currently by Republican Darrell Issa). I’m so excited to welcome voters in areas like Julian and Lakeside and I’ve loved being out on the campaign trail and meeting new folks already.
And it’s not just my race I’m focused on — over the next seven months or so, I’m going to be reaching out to this team about important races to track and ways to get involved all over the country.
But today, I’m asking my strongest supporters to chip in to my own re-election campaign to boost our April fundraising numbers. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
I don’t reach out about fundraising too often, but the fact is that we’re behind where we need to be for the month, and getting back on track has a big impact on what we can do between now and November.
Representing CA-51 in Congress is a huge honor — and one I don’t take for granted for a single second. I’ll keep getting out on the campaign trail this year to listen to voters about their concerns and priorities, and share how I plan to support them if I’m elected to serve a fourth term.
If you can, please consider contributing to my re-election campaign so I can keep up this work and make sure I’m ready to deliver a strong victory in November. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]

The move came just six weeks after the FBI raided an elections office outside Atlanta, seizing records related to the 2020 presidential election. This is because Trump and his cronies continue to spread debunked conspiracy theories about voter fraud in that election.
Arizona’s Maricopa County — like Georgia’s Fulton County — has long been a centerpiece of those conspiracy theories, with opponents of voting rights alleging widespread fraud in the 2020 election without evidence , even after multiple taxpayer-funded state investigations have found nothing.
Trump's MAGA DOJ is partly doing this to salve Trump's wounded ego over his 2020 loss. But they are also doing this to scare eligible voters away from participating in the crucial 2026 midterm elections.

Friend, my experience has prepared me for this moment. **_The toxic politics of Washington are leaving working families and regular Americans behind, and we desperately need change._** I joined this race for Congress over a year ago with the goal of getting to D.C. to cut through the noise and do what I've always done best—solve problems and deliver real results. **As an EPA worker,** I protected our land and water by stopping the dumping of toxic chemical waste in the United States and along the U.S.-Mexico border. **And as a Nevada County supervisor,** I've worked to provide solutions to homelessness, public safety, and the need for more economic opportunities. Friend, I moved to Grass Valley from the Bay Area over 20 years ago to raise my two boys as a single mother, and I'm ready to do whatever it takes to protect the place I'm so grateful to call home from Trump's extremism, ICE, greedy corporations, and toxic politicians. | | | Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.

[ ](https://heidihall.us/l/TogzSwgTYHZO)

Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.

After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.

Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

These far-right politicians seem to believe that if they repeat a lie often enough, people will believe it without a second thought. I know you’ve heard them too, Derek.
When JD Vance came to our Commonwealth to push his Administration’s talking points, he thought he could convince folks to ignore the rising prices at the grocery store and the layoffs that are a direct result of their policies.
**But Pennsylvanians are a whole lot smarter than JD Vance gives us credit for.**
Folks can see the progress we’ve made here at the state level — record funding for public education, hundreds of repaired bridges, and the only growing economy in the Northeast. And Derek, folks can see the chaos, cruelty, and corruption coming out of Washington on a daily basis.

body:
Hi Derek,

I have an important message for you: Thank you.

This campaign isn’t just about me — it’s about showing the strength of the incredible movement we’ve created for a better, stronger Pennsylvania.

Thank you for trusting me to fight for you in D.C., for standing by me through every tough race, and for showing up when it matters most.

From serving on the Scranton School Board to working in the PA Auditor General’s office to serving as Mayor of Scranton (Paige Against the Machine forever!) — my mission has always been to take on corruption and put our families, neighbors, and communities first.

My public service has been dedicated to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in government.

Now, I’m ready to take that fight to a place that needs it badly: a Congress controlled by special interests and self-serving politicians who put the people last.

Whether you’ve supported us financially or are supporting our campaign in other ways, you’ve proven that people power beats big money and Washington special interests every time. If you can, consider chipping in now to bring us one step closer to winning this race.

Thanks for being part of my team,

Paige Cognetti

body:
After GOP vote to close primary: Clerks warn timing could complicate June election
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
FIRST OF ALL, there’s a lot happening in Colorado’s governor’s race right now. We’re asking you: what questions do you want answered by the Republican primary candidates? [Submit your questions here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—we’ll take them directly to the candidates!
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Also, don't miss our deep-dive video on [AG Phil Weiser's claim of "leading" 64 lawsuits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Senators approved [new regulations on gun stores](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—including stricter security, recordkeeping, and fines up to $75,000—sending the bill to Gov. Polis, while budget tensions grow over a [proposal to withhold TABOR refunds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to address a $306 million gap. Broader debates continue as lawmakers clash over [rising spending and priorities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), including funding for migrant healthcare.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A state report found [oversight failures at autism therapy centers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with $78 million in improper Medicaid payments and abuse complaints tied to unregulated facilities. Election officials warn a GOP push to close primaries could [disrupt the June election timeline](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while scrutiny grows over [media reporting on ICE data](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and Attorney General [Weiser’s lawsuit record](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and office performance.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Rep. Lauren Boebert is pushing a bill to [block taxpayer-funded pensions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for lawmakers convicted of crimes, while DNI Tulsi Gabbard has [referred figures tied to the Trump impeachment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for possible criminal investigation. Separately, concern is rising over [multiple deaths or disappearances of scientists](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) linked to sensitive U.S. programs, with no coordinated investigation reported.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, April 17, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[After GOP vote to close primary: Clerks warn timing could complicate June election](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado Republicans left Pueblo with more than a slate of candidates. They left with a plan to change who votes—and how soon that could happen.
At the state assembly, delegates backed a legal push to stop Republican ballots from going out to unaffiliated voters. Republican National Committeeman Randy Corporon and attorney John Eastman are expected to file an injunction in court this week.
The primary is set for June 30. At this point, it’s not about whether Republicans want a closed primary. It’s whether it can happen in time.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Weiser’s Record: The Lawsuit Machine and the Scorecard](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Most lawsuits led by other states:** Of 64 federal lawsuits cited by Attorney General Phil Weiser, only four list Colorado as the lead plaintiff, while 52 were filed and led by other states, raising questions about how the record is presented.
* **“Wins” largely preliminary and ongoing:** Many outcomes cited as successes are temporary injunctions rather than final rulings, and some funding tied to those cases has not yet been delivered despite court orders.
* **Performance gaps reported within AG’s office:** State reports show missed targets across key functions—including consumer protection, criminal appeals, and special prosecutions—alongside growing caseloads and resource constraints.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Colorado budget battle reveals deep divide over spending priorities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **State spending continues to rise despite deficit concerns:** Colorado’s budget increased from $43.6 billion to about $46.6 billion year over year, with overall spending up roughly 44% since 2019—far outpacing population growth.
* **Migrant healthcare programs driving higher costs:** Programs providing subsidized healthcare to undocumented immigrants have expanded significantly, with costs rising well beyond initial projections and enrollment growing into the tens of thousands.
* **Budget debate highlights competing priorities:** Republicans pushed to cap program growth and redirect funding to services like disability care, while Democrats rejected limits and expanded coverage, underscoring ongoing disagreements over spending priorities and resource allocation.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[What tax day looks like in Colorado: A business owner, a paycheck—and what changed this year](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | APRIL 15** _A mother approached a federal official after a recent event with a simple observation. She said her daughter, who is working through nursing school, saved about $8,000 because of the no-tax-on-tips provision. “That’s three to four months of rent,” U.S. Small Business Administration Regional Administrator Justin Everett said, recalling the conversation._ __
**[Where did your TABOR refund go? Follow the spending](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY REP. CALDWELL & REP. EVANS | COMMENTARY | APRIL 15** _TABOR, otherwise known as the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights, was created to protect Coloradans from bloated government spending, prevent politicians from overtaxing working families, and ensure extra revenue is returned to the people who earned it. But under Governor Polis’ fiscal mismanagement and runaway spending, Coloradans are paying the price — through dramatically reduced TABOR refunds this year and no refunds at all next year.___
**[Less Pay. Less Jobs. Businesses Blame Overregulation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | APRIL 15** _Colorado has spent five years building one of the most expansive labor regulatory environments in the country. Paid family leave. Wage transparency requirements. A lowered standard for harassment claims. Minimum wages that rise automatically every year, with several cities setting their own higher rates on top. Each law arrived with the same promise: this is good for workers._
__

The important thing is to establish a political climate of opinion which will make it politically profitable for the wrong people to do the right thing. Unless it is politically profitable for the wrong people to do the right thing, the right people will not do the right thing either, or if they try, they will shortly be out of office." – Milton Friedman

name: Sarah Elfreth
subject: ICE is not a weapon.
disclaimer_text:
Paid for by
Elfreth for Maryland
body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]
Friend,

When I first stood at the doors of the Baltimore ICE facility in July 2025, I was denied entry. But I don’t take no for an answer when it comes to the safety and dignity of our neighbors.

That’s why I've returned to the facility twice since then — to stand up and hold the government accountable to us, the people. Just a few weeks ago, when I went for a third time, I brought forward the critical issues you’ve sent to me and my office: from access to legal counsel and medication to the terrifying rate at which people with no criminal record are being taken off the street by undertrained, masked agents.

When I took the oath of office to represent Maryland’s Third District, I promised to be a voice for every member of our community. That duty is more than just voting on the House floor — it requires active, rigorous oversight to ensure our government remains accountable to the people it serves.

As your Congresswoman, I will do everything in my power to end the weaponization of ICE and the inhumane way this Administration is treating our neighbors. This behavior has no place in our communities.

That’s why my team and I are working hand in hand with local leaders, community advocates, and partners at every level to ensure our neighbors remain safe. If you or a loved one needs assistance with ICE or any federal agency, please reach out to my staff at my DC office at (410) 832-8890. We’re here to listen and to help.

Onward,

Sarah Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. name: Josefine Jaynes, Team WIWFP
subject: A political shockwave in Wisconsin
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
Last week, working class candidates across the state delivered a landslide of wins. Out of the 38 that we ran, 32 of them brought home victories, even in rural towns and Republican strongholds. | | | Hey Peter, this is Josefine, an organizer for WFP in Wisconsin. Last week, working class candidates across the state delivered a _landslide_ of wins. Out of the 38 that we ran, **32 of them brought home victories,** even in rural towns and Republican strongholds. This didn't happen by accident. Voters are fed up with politics as usual — and our candidates and volunteers did the work, having real conversations with people in their communities every single day. And those conversations revealed something important: people are paying attention to what's happening in their backyards, and they're ready to push back. One issue that came up again and again? **The rapid expansion of AI data centers.** Over the last few years, massive tech companies have swarmed my home state like vultures, spending billions of dollars to buy our land and pillage our natural resources. And far too many of our elected officials have been more than happy to support it. **But this year, voters drew a line.** In Menomonie, WFP candidate Matthew Crowe unseated the 16-year incumbent mayor who, with Republican backers, supported a proposed data center that’s projected to consume 75,000 gallons of water per day. Voters in Port Washington just passed the nation’s first-ever referendum to restrict future data centers.1 And across the state, nearly 70% of Wisconsin voters believe that the costs of these construction projects outweigh the benefits.2 **[The tide is turning, Peter. AI and crypto billionaires thought they could dupe working families in Wisconsin and failed. clean_body: Last week, working class candidates across the state delivered a landslide of wins. Out of the 38 that we ran, 32 of them brought home victories, even in rural towns and Republican strongholds. | | | Hey Peter, this is Josefine, an organizer for WFP in Wisconsin. Last week, working class candidates across the state delivered a landslide of wins. Out of the 38 that we ran, 32 of them brought home victories, even in rural towns and Republican strongholds. This didn't happen by accident. Voters are fed up with politics as usual — and our candidates and volunteers did the work, having real conversations with people in their communities every single day. And those conversations revealed something important: people are paying attention to what's happening in their backyards, and they're ready to push back. One issue that came up again and again? The rapid expansion of AI data centers. Over the last few years, massive tech companies have swarmed my home state like vultures, spending billions of dollars to buy our land and pillage our natural resources. And far too many of our elected officials have been more than happy to support it. But this year, voters drew a line. In Menomonie, WFP candidate Matthew Crowe unseated the 16-year incumbent mayor who, with Republican backers, supported a proposed data center that’s projected to consume 75,000 gallons of water per day. Voters in Port Washington just passed the nation’s first-ever referendum to restrict future data centers.1 And across the state, nearly 70% of Wisconsin voters believe that the costs of these construction projects outweigh the benefits.2 These fights weren’t isolated — they were part of a broader shift. People are rejecting a system that prioritizes corporate profits over their communities. Even in small, rural, and historically-Republican parts of the state, we helped elect a deep bench of leaders who are ready to fight for affordable housing, health care, and an end to ICE’s violence. WFP-endorsed Judge Chris Taylor beat her opponent with 60% of the vote, creating a 5-2 progressive majority on the Wisconsin Supreme Court. All SIX of our top-of-ticket candidates — Mayors and City Council Presidents — won, in places like Waukesha, where Alicia Halvensleben is the first non-Republican aligned leader in years, as well as in Eau Claire, and Fitchburg. And another six WFP-endorsed candidates won seats on the La Crosse County Board — ensuring 50-50 gender parity for the first time in history. This was our first year organizing in many of these places, too. And it’s only the beginning. WFP is bringing these same values and organizing tactics to towns and cities all over the country. We forced a runoff. Now we finish it. |

If we win, we take a powerful step toward leveling the playing field and giving voters the final say. That is why your support at this moment is so critical. body:
I want to introduce you to something my team and I have been working on.
#

Team,
It’s no secret we’ve got to take back majorities in both the House and Senate this year. To do that, I want to introduce you to something my team and I have been working on.
It’s called **Liftoff PAC** , and it’s the organization I started to provide direct support to the people who will help us win back those majorities.
We’ll be doing a number of things to get the job done, including a bunch of travel and events. But one of the most important things we’ll be doing is contributing directly to those candidates.
I know a thing or two about winning tough races, and I know how important that financial support can be when it really matters. It can close your budget gap, share your message more widely, get more people knocking doors, or even something as simple as putting pizza on the table for your volunteers at 11 o’clock the night before Election Day.
We’re backing candidates we’re confident in, the people putting together strong teams in places we need to win. For them, donations like these can make all the difference.
Now, if you want to help me win back those majorities, can I ask you something?

##### APRIL 17, 2026 | DERELICTIONS DOSSIER | VOLUME 3
### **The Core Charge**
Representative Daniel Webster, who serves Florida's 11th District, has adopted the posture of The Parched Sentry. His is a policy of letting wells run dry. On the issue of water and land rights, he stands watch but will not engage the enemy. His publicly stated policy--that it is "inappropriate" to "compel an agency to decide an issue in your favor"--is a formal surrender of his constitutional duty to check executive overreach. This dossier exposes this record of surrender across Florida's 11th District, contrasts it with his self-congratulatory "constituent service," and presents our strategic response: the Administrative Independence Act, powered by a citizen evidence-gathering operation.
* * *
### **I. The Confession: A Record of Surrender**
**Source:** Rep. Daniel Webster's Official Website, "Help with a Federal Agency"
**Verbatim Quote:**_" My staff is happy to ask for information or a status report on a pending case, or ask for clarification on the reasons for denial, but it would be inappropriate for me to compel any agency to decide an issue in your favor, or attempt to overturn a decision that is final."_
**Analysis:** This is not a humble admission of limited power; it is the codification of a failed philosophy. Webster frames aggressive representation--advocating for a constituent against an administrative agency--as "inappropriate." He reduces his office's role to that of a polite intermediary, a requestor of "status reports," while the agencies wield the power of final, unchallengeable decree. This **record of surrender** provides the philosophical cover for fifteen years of inaction as the regulatory state expanded its reach into private property.
* * *
### **II. The Performance: Managing Surrender**
While declaring himself powerless against agency actions, Representative Webster actively publicizes his success in managing the bureaucratic process _after_ the harm is done.
**Evidence A: The $3.6 Million Boast**
* **Source:** _The Webster Wire_ Newsletter, January 12, 2026.
* **Claim:** "In 2025 alone, my office successfully returned over $3.6 million owed to constituents from federal agencies..."
* **Context:** This is hailed as effective "constituent service." In reality, it highlights a perverse system: his office helps citizens recover money **the federal government wrongly took from them in the first place**. He treats the symptom (a delayed refund) while ignoring the disease (an overbearing, error-prone bureaucracy with the power to seize assets without due process).

**Evidence B: Funding the Pipes, Overlooking the Hazard**
* **Source:** Same newsletter, January 12, 2026.
* **Claim:** Celebrates securing funding for "City of Clermont for Stormwater Infrastructure Improvements," "Polk City for Wastewater Improvement Project," and "City of Wildwood for Wastewater Capacity Upgrades."
* **Context:** These are laudable infrastructure projects. Yet, his failure lies in the contradiction: He promotes his role in funding the government while surrendering to that government's power to devalue the property rights of the people whom those funds are meant to serve. He builds the infrastructure but legitimizes the confiscation.

* * *
### **III. The Consequence: A District Forfeited**
Webster's **record of surrender** is not an abstract policy; it has concrete, devastating consequences across FL-11. The following are archetypes based on the established legal authority of the agencies involved:
* **Polk County:** A farmer receives a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers "Jurisdictional Determination" letter declaring his pasture a "Water of the United States (WOTUS)." His use of his land is frozen. Webster's office will "ask for clarification."
* **Lake County:** A citrus grower is mandated by the St. Johns River Water Management District (SJRWMD) to adhere to strict nutrient loading limits, dictating how he manages his grove. The District acts as rule-maker, investigator, and judge. Webster's office will "request a status report."
* **Sumter County:** A landowner's water withdrawal is restricted by the Southwest Florida Water Management District's (SWFWMD) "Minimum Flows and Levels" (MFLs) for the Withlacoochee River. The agency that sets the scientific standard also prosecutes violations. Webster "cannot overturn that decision."
* **Orange County:** A development permit is delayed for years by the Army Corps over WOTUS concerns regarding a drainage ditch in the Econlockhatchee River watershed. The Corps investigates, prosecutes, and adjudicates. Webster "cannot compel them to decide in your favor."

**The Pattern:** In each case, an administrative agency acts as prosecutor, judge, and jury. In each case, Representative Webster's proclaimed remedy is a request for information, not a challenge to the system.
* * *
### **IV. The Strategic Failure: Confusing Leaf-Watering for Root-Striking**
Webster's model of "constituent service" is the political equivalent of watering the leaves of a tree whose roots are infected. He addresses superficial outcomes (getting money returned, funding local projects) while the root cause--a consolidation of legislative, executive, and judicial power in unaccountable agencies--continues to kill the tree.
His tenure is defined by managing the symptoms of a disease he refuses to diagnose. He has become a **Parched Sentry** : posted at the gate, watching as the resources (property rights, water rights) he is sworn to protect are slowly drained away, offering only the hollow consolation of a "status report" on their disappearance.
* * *
### **V. The Palomo Doctrine: Strike the Root, Secure the Table**
The Palomo campaign rejects the **record of surrender** and the **performance** of managed surrender. Our strategy is the Strike-Secure Protocol.
**The Strike: The Administrative Independence Act**
This legislation abolishes the internal courts of federal agencies like the EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers. It forces any dispute over a permit denial, fine, or jurisdictional determination into an Article III federal court, where the citizen is guaranteed a trial by jury under the Seventh Amendment.
* **Philosophical Foundation:** Alexander Hamilton called the jury trial a "valuable privilege" and a "security against corruption." James Madison's "double security" for rights is nullified when one entity holds all power.
* **Outcome:** It changes the incentive. An agency must now prove its case to a jury of citizens, replacing bureaucratic fiat with public justification.

**The Secure: The District 11 Evidence File**
We are building an irrefutable case, not for an agency's review, but for Congress to act.
* **Action 1: Gather Your Evidence.** (WOTUS letters, permit denials, enforcement actions).
* **Action 2: Personalize The Cost.** (Narrative of impact on family, livelihood, inheritance).
* **Action 3: Send Us The Proof.** (To **[evidence@americankitchentable.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/14c71395-6254-4668-b933-406247a60b69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**)

Once in Congress, this evidence will form the backbone of the legislative push for the Administrative Independence Act. We do not ask for a "status report"; we compile the evidence for a verdict.
* * *
### **VI. Call to Action: From Parched Sentry to Active Defender**
The choice before the voters of District 11 is not between two styles of constituent service. It is between two philosophies of power:
1. **The Webster Model:** Accept administrative supremacy. Seek clarification, request reports, and manage outcomes within a broken system.
2. **The Palomo Model:** Restore constitutional balance. Strike at the root of agency overreach and secure fundamental rights through structural reform.

We are recruiting citizen-witnesses to build this case. Your evidence is our ammunition. Your story is the testimony that will compel Congress to act.
**Strike the root. Secure the table.**
Forward, Always.
Ivette Palomo
Champion of the American Kitchen Table

Team, Baseball is back, and there is nothing in this world that beats Fenway Park in the Spring. The sounds, the smells, the references that only avid fans can understand and appreciate. It's perfect. Fenway is the oldest ballpark in America, and we love it for that. But we also love it because the people who run it had the sense to make changes when they were needed. With new seats, better lighting, and upgraded concourses, they kept the soul of the place but made it work for the people showing up today, not just the people who showed up in 1912. And because of the care and thoughtfulness by which they did it, nobody looked at those renovations and thought the changes were disrespecting decades of greatness. Instead, they said, "Finally." There is a parallel here with Washington. The institution matters, what it stands for matters, but the infrastructure is failing, and the whole operation feels like it was built for a different era because it was. Loving something and demanding better from it aren't opposites. Red Sox fans have known that forever, and it's time we applied the same standard to our government. clean_body: Memorial Day 2026: Honor our veterans with me| | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. body:
Viktor Orbán, long a symbol of democratic backsliding, was defeated by the very force he worked so hard to bend: the will of the voters.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Viktor Orbán, long a symbol of democratic backsliding and the self-proclaimed creator of "illiberal democracy," was defeated by the very force he worked so hard to bend: the will of the voters. In Hungary, citizens were given a chance to speak clearly, and they did. Their message was bigger than one man. It was a reminder that even leaders who spend years weakening institutions, centralizing power, and putting themselves above the public are still vulnerable when people decide enough is enough. This was not only a vote about ideology. It was also a vote about accountability. Orbán’s defeat reflected something basic but powerful: people expect leaders to serve the public, not themselves. When governments become arrogant, insulated, corrupt, or indifferent to the daily struggles of ordinary families, voters notice. And when democracy is still strong enough to give them a voice, they can use it to demand something better. That is why Hungary’s election matters far beyond Hungary. It stands as a warning to leaders everywhere, including here in the United States, that public office is not personal property. It is a temporary trust. Leaders are sent to their capitals to solve problems, uphold democratic norms, and improve people’s lives. When they fail in that responsibility, voters not only can replace them; they _should_ replace them. At Forward, we believe politics should be rooted in service, responsibility, and results. We are working to support leaders who understand that holding office means stewardship, not self-preservation. Hungary may be the latest example of voters insisting on that standard, but it cannot be the last. In this election year, we will keep fighting to make sure more leaders are chosen not for their ambition but for their willingness to serve. **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**

Featuring Deke Copenhaver, former mayor of Augusta, Georgia, Brian Vincent, current mayor of Farmville, Virginia, and Clint Eisenhauer, South Carolina Forward Party Chair, the episode explores what it looks like to lead with service, accountability, and community-first thinking. These leaders share firsthand experiences navigating political pressure, earning trust at the grassroots level, and making decisions that directly shape the lives of their constituents. A former presidential candidate came to the New Mexico state Capitol on Friday to announce a new home for voters who are tired of the strife between Republicans and Democrats. “Politics in the state will never be the same,” Andrew Yang proclaimed to about two dozen people at a news conference where he announced the arrival of the Forward Party.
### [Andrew Yang Urges Action at Forward Party Utah Convention](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=zU_Iszns4qSlfpGzVVRDZcZoveqA8EQprEvnB7zsNFHZSiU42c1MiMPD-joxVsTB3N6dPGOMyfMRaPe3LDxApo68SU26mOAq54FCoteuwD9ddeLFAExiZMF6j5OpsfI8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_99a&n=10)
If you’ve spent any time watching the American political landscape lately, you know the feeling of staring at a ballot and feeling like you’re being asked to choose between two versions of the same headache. For a lot of voters in the Beehive State, that frustration has moved past a quiet grumble and into a full-blown movement. We’re seeing it play out in Utah, where the Forward Party isn’t just knocking on doors—they’re attempting to rewrite the rules of engagement in a state traditionally known as a Republican stronghold.

Peter,

President Trump and his allies in Congress are pushing the SAVE Act, legislation that would require voters to present a passport or certified birth certificate just to register to vote.

**This is not about election security. This is about making it harder for people to vote.**

[Voting rights are under attack at the federal level, and we cannot sit back and let it happen. Will you sign my petition to stand with me in defense of every Rhode Islander’s right to vote?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129676969/615156215/-1202839903?source=EM_NBI_SM_20260417_PT_righttovote_0_3MO_Sethmagaziner_NA_NA_NA&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZTRiZTJiNC05ZTNhLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OnmSTthWweOfVHF0rJcw2J-InmZoro700OHHZNKUD_M=&emci=86a932e1-9a3a-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=be4be2b4-9e3a-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=15384964) | | **[SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129676970/615156216/-1202839903?source=EM_NBI_SM_20260417_PT_righttovote_0_3MO_Sethmagaziner_NA_NA_NA&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcyMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZTRiZTJiNC05ZTNhLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OnmSTthWweOfVHF0rJcw2J-InmZoro700OHHZNKUD_M=&emci=86a932e1-9a3a-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=be4be2b4-9e3a-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=15384964)**

The SAVE Act would turn away millions of voters. Married women whose names no longer match their birth certificates could be denied the right to vote. Friend, In my state of Michigan, Black maternal mortality rates are among the highest in the nation—with Black women 4.5 times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes than white women, and Black infants 3 times more likely to die than white infants. Solutions to this urgent crisis include investing in more Black healthcare providers and more birth centers, which are midwife-led, home-like places that have been proven to improve maternal and infant health outcomes. **The Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice (MCRJ) is advancing Black maternal health through grassroots leadership, policy advocacy, and coalition building.** MCRJ is committed to ensuring that all people receive the dignified, equitable care they deserve before, during, and after birth. As the policy lead for the Michigan State of Birth Justice Coalition, MCRJ grounds its work in the foundational leadership of Birth Detroit—home to the only Black-led birth center in the state. The coalition’s community-rooted vision has helped shape critical policy wins, including a newly signed law to license and expand access to birth centers, and the “Michigan Momnibus” policy package—featuring vital bills to support doulas and midwives and protect patients from discrimination. [**During this Black Maternal Health Week, will you make an urgent donation of $5 to support the Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice’s life-saving advocacy to eradicate racial disparities in maternal and infant health? Stand up for Black moms now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJk1mZ834WYhJDLS2P_zfAXG0wgplUfSThfBt_4Cj29kIykkoIDQy91iBpOM3aPCycnmeZXVqAL7INbOBm8x_IjuWp-ej_B8oNAPC5kPHFbweVuKKyqGB67T0TioB9xj-unkhwQIcg_PHv-JxTQigd0v7QHYd6jR0Xks2tgKGKzDuG0xH05-h8BqOhxu8wu_CPwmDcxoRC0Wv0PnKZCwDymr7mgdHNSp27qoJrgW80AboagndK58h61blaEW8DOyA81Th7hfjVX2q2hPxGnPptBcuZIYDMY0ikLCFCXII_xHCbYQr9qhWHlMKZwYBq4co2VnQvvBWldEmF_tdTtfCYwuSvv_6GohqYNq0_lDDAefru6tdUsgGAapMjVW0Pynvg/4pv/RJ29unT7QyS7k2PuAQ52xg/h1/h001.GnhWtLKUkzAd-3JUzhxz8HdaBGKWnZu4WmuMYTaS-EA) | [DONATE TO MCRJ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJk1mZ834WYhJDLS2P_zfAXNauryzu2xdiNe8dtVgECQHcNEwq7IQoFbDSh2IQisu7V4OmdkcPEXZmtUDHKRBJWQQ6Amf0QAF1Wz18Is8cMSFjiPW3gRXZH7AMFqooQlzgUYxcNuFBmxeUMqMXP4U4R3GZDFKHfausCcm7WTqyMRfSJgq7HR20ZXTzz12NO2IMGsYBE2rPeRel5gO-vMFBV_aVSk2WxmqhDVZssTEiETTI3lJcCSa277zbJq6gqok7EEa-KUIEIMAQMW97mvPokhVX1DVa4J0KUVcMA70GVDbNo_iS7frWTvNnqENBgkqPCCi1fzuikaqyvonLZzU4jjv2ZFp9fzy46iD7yZI-oi9ahXxyFF6dRHfrXQHcvWZE/4pv/RJ29unT7QyS7k2PuAQ52xg/h2/h001.S4lLaSHq5Umv2EqQ_oSmbd_Q8db1P123ehxAsuu4GpA)

Thanks in part to the relentless advocacy from the Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice, the Michigan State Senate introduced and passed the “Michigan Momnibus” package during last year’s Black Maternal Health Week. Now MCRJ is working to demand a vote in the Michigan State House.
While pushing for life-saving policies, the Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice is also providing education and resources to communities, families, healthcare providers, and the institutions that shape their care experiences.
This community group’s work is rooted in reproductive justice, which is the human right to maintain personal bodily autonomy, to have children or not have children, and to parent in safe, sustainable communities.
In addition to birth justice, MCRJ advocates for intersecting issues such as environmental justice and housing justice—recognizing that access to clean water, safe housing, and economic stability is essential to true reproductive freedom. This includes women who are birthing while in custody, where autonomy and care are often constrained by carceral systems.
The Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice’s critical work depends on federal resources to expand access to doulas, midwives, and culturally competent care. **Cuts by conservatives in Congress and illegal funding freezes by this administration make the need for grassroots donations even more critical to ensure that communities don’t lose access to life-saving support.**

Rashida

The Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice (MCRJ) is advancing Black maternal health through grassroots leadership, policy advocacy, and coalition building. MCRJ is committed to ensuring that all people receive the dignified, equitable care they deserve before, during, and after birth. As the policy lead for the Michigan State of Birth Justice Coalition, MCRJ grounds its work in the foundational leadership of Birth Detroit—home to the only Black-led birth center in the state. The coalition’s community-rooted vision has helped shape critical policy wins, including a newly signed law to license and expand access to birth centers, and the “Michigan Momnibus” policy package—featuring vital bills to support doulas and midwives and protect patients from discrimination. | Thanks in part to the relentless advocacy from the Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice, the Michigan State Senate introduced and passed the “Michigan Momnibus” package during last year’s Black Maternal Health Week. Now MCRJ is working to demand a vote in the Michigan State House. While pushing for life-saving policies, the Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice is also providing education and resources to communities, families, healthcare providers, and the institutions that shape their care experiences. This community group’s work is rooted in reproductive justice, which is the human right to maintain personal bodily autonomy, to have children or not have children, and to parent in safe, sustainable communities. In addition to birth justice, MCRJ advocates for intersecting issues such as environmental justice and housing justice—recognizing that access to clean water, safe housing, and economic stability is essential to true reproductive freedom. This includes women who are birthing while in custody, where autonomy and care are often constrained by carceral systems. The Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice’s critical work depends on federal resources to expand access to doulas, midwives, and culturally competent care. Cuts by conservatives in Congress and illegal funding freezes by this administration make the need for grassroots donations even more critical to ensure that communities don’t lose access to life-saving support. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, with 100% going directly to Michigan Chamber for Reproductive Justice | | | | | | | | | Thank you. Our systems and institutions have failed to provide Black people with the high-quality healthcare that everyone deserves. But I refuse to accept this status quo, and I thank you for standing with me and the movement for health equity. In Congress, I’m supporting policies for Black maternal and infant health like the federal Momnibus Act , and I’m working with the Congressional Mamas’ Caucus to center Black mothers and other mothers of color in policymaking. Together, we will continue demanding and building a society that honors everyone’s safety, dignity, and bodily autonomy. What we're watching right now across our government is a mess.

The Trump administration is treating governance like a punchline. The GOP is making never-ending chaotic decisions, pushing deeply unserious priorities, and a steady stream of headlines that would be unbelievable if they weren't happening in real time.

And while the noise gets louder, working people are the ones paying the price. Costs are up, stability feels shaky, trust in our democracy is being chipped away day by day, and unless you're one of Trump's well-connected, deep-pocketed buddies, it's getting harder to feel like the system is even built for you anymore. body:
Trump and the GOP want to pay for this illegal war by taking health care away from even more Americans. |
---
Donald Trump is using this war to distract from the Epstein files, Peter, and the American people are paying the price: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129678260/615160360/-1870630518?refcode=AU_DSG_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260417_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOTMwYTllYS1hMDNhLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jYG89_MFHiCFL1w3f3QjAaAt_Om0p80F3OozlFECEfs=) The Pentagon has asked for — and the House GOP appears ready to accept — as much as _$200 billion_ to fund Trump’s illegal war. **They want to pay for it by taking health care away from even more Americans.** Their cuts to Medicaid are projected to force nearly 8 million people out of the program in the next eight years. In the past three months, more than 2 million people had to drop their Affordable Care Act plans because Republicans refused to extend enhanced subsidies. This war is driving up costs of everything — gas and groceries — on top of the affordability crisis and inflation fueled by Trump’s tariffs. Businesses are pulling back and job losses are on the horizon. And the GOP? They’re twiddling their thumbs while Trump plays games with the economy and national security — again. Let’s be clear: **Trump’s actions, in war and in the economy, are not for the benefit of the American people — not by a longshot. They are intended to fulfill one purpose: distract us from the Department of Justice’s massive cover-up of the Epstein files in order to conceal Donald Trump’s involvement.** Trump is isolating us globally and hurting Americans at home. name: Citizens Alliance New Hampshire
subject: Voice Your Support for Home Education Freedom!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CITIZENS ALLIANCE OF NEW HAMPSHIRE]()
body:
HB 1268 amends RSA 193-A, New Hampshire's home education statute, to provide greater flexibility and autonomy for parents who choose to homeschool...

| | | | | [|
---](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=ce9e02206a&e=8c8e704ee6)
| | | | | | Peter,

Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire is mobilizing for another key battle in defense of parental rights and educational freedom. House Bill 1268, the "Home Education Freedom Act," is scheduled for a public hearing in the Senate Education Committee on Tuesday, April 21st, at 9:45 a.m. in the Map Room at the State Library.

**We need as many voices as possible to testify and let the Senate Education Committee know you fully support HB 1268.**

This bill represents a major step toward reducing unnecessary government oversight on homeschooling families and empowering parents to direct their children's education without burdensome red tape.

**HB 1268 amends RSA 193-A, New Hampshire's home education statute, to provide greater flexibility and autonomy for parents who choose to homeschool.**

**MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD!**
[ Click here to go to the Senate remote testimony/sign-in page right now and follow these steps:](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=2cd2092c71&e=8c8e704ee6)

➡️ Select the date (April 21, 2026) for the hearing.
➡️ Choose the Senate Education Committee
➡️ Select HB 1268.
➡️ Select “I am a Member of the Public.”
➡️ Select “I’m Representing Myself.”
➡️ Indicate your position: **“I Support this Bill.”** ➡️ Click “Continue” and enter your Personal Information.
➡️ In the optional testimony field, write your own brief message (upload a PDF or type directly).➡️ Review and submit before the sign-in closes.
➡️ [Click here to go to the Senate Education Committee page.](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=a7637ad62e&e=8c8e704ee6)
➡️ Click “**Email Entire Committee** ” and submit your written testimony.
---
[|
---](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=024a49aefa&e=8c8e704ee6)
| [CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR REMOTE TESTIMONY >>>](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=cdd0abf7ae&e=8c8e704ee6)
---
| | **Suggestions for Your Testimony
** _**(Write Your Own – Committees Notice Personalized Messages)**_
✅ Let the Senate Education Committee know you support the passage of House Bill 1268

✅ Share why parental choice in education matters to you, your family, or New Hampshire's future.

✅ Emphasize that parents, not the government, know best how to educate their children.

✅ Highlight how reducing notifications and making evaluations voluntary removes unnecessary burdens without sacrificing accountability.

✅ Note the bill's role in protecting family autonomy and aligning with our state's tradition of limited government.

✅ Mention the importance of homeschool flexibility for working families, special needs children, or those seeking tailored learning.

Keep your message heartfelt and specific. Committees pay more attention to unique voices than identical copies.

_**We need all hands on deck!**_

Forward this email to homeschooling parents, grandparents, and fellow liberty supporters across New Hampshire. Every supportive sign-in helps!
Let’s keep New Hampshire the Live Free or Die State our children deserve!

For New Hampshire,
---
[|
---](https://citizensalliancenh.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9ec7dd6f72fe3fc1550cd2695&id=2ebdeaeea6&e=8c8e704ee6)

body:
Two-thirds don’t feel represented |
#

Team, Last week, we asked you a simple question: _**Do you feel represented by your elected leaders?**_ Two-thirds of respondents said no. **Only one-third said yes.** That shouldn’t sit comfortably with any of us. If most people don’t feel heard, then something is broken. And it’s not going to fix itself by waiting for the same system to produce different results. That is exactly why Governor Whitmer is focused on recruiting and electing a new generation of leaders with Fight Like Hell PAC. We’re focused on supporting and training leaders who actually come from their communities, who listen, and who will put in the work instead of just talking about it. But here’s the part that matters. Two-thirds of people feeling unrepresented is a problem. The work to change that takes real resources, and it’s happening now. body:
I visited Texas A&M yesterday.
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240797%2E444211%2EvUihjR)
I visited Texas A&M yesterday. I kept hearing about academic freedom. I met A&M philosophy professor Dr. Martin Peterson who was not allowed to teach.... PLATO!! in his PHILOSOPHY class because the Symposium includes descriptions of homosexual love. Find this outrageous? Join the protest on Monday, details included on the flyer that Leah is holding:

Our volunteer Ken told me about working for USAID for 16 years, all over the world...Mozambique, Liberia, Bangladesh. He’s an aquatic disease specialist. Happy he’s keeping his public service going with us.

Met Briana who reminded me that we first met in Garden City (Glasscock County) in 2018 (now/then):

Paige told me she was studying physics and I told her I’m fascinated by this stuff, but it’s beyond my comprehension. Is light a wave or a particle? She said “it’s neither more than it’s both” — which blew my mind and left me more confused. She said check out A&M professor Tatiana, she’s the GOAT. I did and she is. (Tatiana Erukhimova).
Liliana told me about a friend in Dallas whose dad was picked up and deported and how scared people in her community are. She asked me “What do I tell her?” I said, tell her we’re with her, we’re doing the work to make sure our laws and actions match our values. Registering and turning out young people is key to that.
Ronin said hi and I said like the De Niro movie where he removes the bullet himself? Yes, it means “lone warrior” but she’s not alone.
Emaan is spending the summer interning for the Muslim Public Affairs Council in DC and will volunteer for us when she comes back in the fall.
Freshman Leaders in Christ approached me as I was on my way out and asked if there was anything that I would like them to pray for. I said how about an end to the divisions in this country, to the rampant corruption, to the wars that we wage. How about praying for peace?
The young man leading us said a beautiful and powerful prayer. Afterward we talked about the mysteries of science and religion (“it’s neither more than it’s both”), the goodness that’s out there and our desire for people to be kind to each other.

Big thanks to team PXP and A&M students. Gig em!

More soon,
Beto

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

| | | | | |

Friends,
We wanted to follow up on our earlier message — we still need your help!
We're getting closer to the 15th Annual KHTS Santa Clarita Home & Garden Show, and we're still looking for volunteers to staff the Jason Gibbs for Congress booth. If you've been thinking about getting involved, now is the time.
**Saturday, April 25th & Sunday, April 26th, 202610:00 AM to 4:00 PM each dayCentral Park, Santa Clarita**
This is one of the biggest community weekends Santa Clarita has to offer. More than 20,000 local residents will come through over the two days. It's a rare chance to meet your neighbors face to face, share Jason's vision for our community, and represent the campaign right here at home.
As a volunteer, you'll:
* Welcome attendees at our booth
* Share Jason's story and his campaign for Congress with community members
* Hand out campaign materials and answer questions

No experience needed. Just bring a friendly attitude and a love for this community.
If you can join us for one or both days, please reply with your name, phone number, and your availability.
This is what grassroots campaigning looks like. Neighbor to neighbor, right here in Santa Clarita.
We hope you'll join us.
Warmly,Jason Gibbs

# Some Exciting Announcements!
Adelita for Congress Newsletter
---
| | Hi Peter,

**Happy Friday!** We wanted to reach out with an exciting announcement and let everyone know that Team Grijalva will be supporting the [**Protect Education Initiative**](https://adelitaforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=4efffbdef3b238a45f56f3bb2&id=9988a9a766&e=f7c3700ccb)**.**
This initiative would bring transparency to the ESA Voucher program and **end reckless spending and fraud** that takes money from education here in Arizona. If this initiative passes, **MILLIONS OF DOLLARS** would go back into our education budget funding public schools across the state.
The [**Protect Education Initiative**](https://adelitaforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=4efffbdef3b238a45f56f3bb2&id=d4e968b9a4&e=f7c3700ccb) is in the signature collection phase so click here to see how you can **get involved** with local efforts across the state.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: A few reflections on the Artemis mission
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
With the incredible success of the recent Artemis mission, it has been such a joy to find our collective awe in something as a nation.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3124%2E21716%2E1E_wu4)
**With the incredible success of the recent Artemis mission, it has been such a joy to find our collective awe in something as a nation.**
It’s been a reminder that these missions not only have scientific value, but a civic, almost spiritual value. They remind us of who we are.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260417-1.f6S0c9&refcode=em20260417-3124&t=2&akid=3124%2E21716%2E1E_wu4)
At a time when our attention spans have been commodified and every force seems to be pulling us apart, these kinds of shared experiences help bond us again into one people. Moments like this can be civically healing — an antidote to the division that seems to define this age.
And it seems to have come just when we needed it most. It’s no wonder that in another age of conflict and chaos, the 1960s, we dreamed of — and reached — the moon.
But unlike the 1960s — which was a decade of tragedy, but also historic progress — this rebirth of space travel not only brings us together, it also helps to solve for one of our current civic crises: the fear that we can’t work together to do big things.
**Instead, humans have now traveled further into space than ever before because we worked together across our differences.** Parts for the Artemis mission were developed in every single state. The public and private sectors collaborated. Government delivered on its promise. And four people from different walks of life lived and worked together to “slip the surly bonds of earth to touch the face of God.”
But the power of space travel isn’t limited to what it reveals about what we can do. It also reveals much about who we are. As the images were beamed back to Earth, I was struck by one in particular. It showed, all in one frame, the window of Orion, the moon, and then, way off in the distance, our small crescent that we call home. Seeing it, you can almost feel the isolation and vulnerability of the four astronauts.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260417-1.f6S0c9&refcode=em20260417-3124&t=3&akid=3124%2E21716%2E1E_wu4)
**It made me feel grateful that I was home.** Lucky that I was with all of you. For all of our sins and foibles, for all the tragedy we can inflict on one another, for all the hate and fear, I love us. I love being here with you all.
Humanity yearns to be near for love, safety, humor, joy, help, and just company. All of us, no matter where we live on that crescent, wants community. And when you have it, it is a gift.
I can't help but feel that so many of our challenges right now stem from the fact that we suppress that gift. We have never been more connected with each other and, yet, we are isolated from one another. We’ve made it so easy to be alone without feeling lonely.
While the platforms that we live on can dull that symptom of loneliness, it only worsens the disease of isolation. And whether you are on the other side of the moon or alone on your phone, the numerical distance itself is not what erodes our happiness. It’s the isolation.
**So as we welcome the four astronauts back to Earth, let us not only continue our quest as humans to go further. Let us also choose to go nearer.**
Let us cherish that gift that we already have. We are here. We can gather. And, in so doing, we can realize our most human of hopes, the hope that exceeds even our quest for exploration or our desire for earthly success: the hope to simply belong.
Thank you for reading,
Sarah McBride

Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs Sean Parnell revealed the Afghanistan Withdrawal Special Review Panel established by Secretary Pete Hegseth at President Donald Trump's direction **[has completed key interviews and reviewed millions of documents](https://substack.com/redirect/01256171-59b9-404f-8ea8-7f5f701228c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for a comprehensive report on the botched 2021 withdrawal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01256171-59b9-404f-8ea8-7f5f701228c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Panel Completes Key Interviews:** The Afghanistan Withdrawal Special Review Panel has completed the substantive phase of its interviews with senior military and civilian leaders including Generals Milley McKenzie and others involved in 2021 withdrawal.
* **Millions Documents Reviewed Thoroughly:** The panel has reviewed more than nine million documents from multiple agencies compared to the previous narrow Department-wide review under Former Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin that examined around three thousand documents.
* **Thirteen Troops Killed Recalled:** Thirteen U.S. troops were killed during the botched withdrawal that occurred under Joe Biden's watch in August 2021 prompting the need for full transparency and accountability.
* **Report Expected Coming Months:** The final report will be delivered to the Secretary of War and the American people in the coming months as the most thorough examination of systemic leadership failures.

* * *
# USA Today fires reporter over Russini criticism
USA Today ended its contractor relationship with sports reporter Crissy Froyd after she **[publicly blasted former reporter for The Athletic Dianna Russini](https://substack.com/redirect/d273c494-4f60-4dd6-a2d5-bae2c5abd486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** accusing her of sleeping with players or coaches for professional gain following Russini's resignation over alleged risque photos with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.

Friend,

Last night, Congress failed to rein in Trump’s authority to wage war in Iran. The War Powers Resolution fell short by just one vote — and it was a Democrat who cast it.

Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) believes it is critical to make sure the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is fully funded ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Britt, Chair of the DHS Appropriations Subcommittee, led a joint hearing with Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), Chair of the Commerce, Justice, and Science (CJS) Appropriations Subcommittee, to review preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. | | U.S. Senators Katie Britt, R-Alabama, and John Fetterman’s, D-Pennsylvania, legislation, the Stop the Scroll Act, which would create a mental health warning label requirement for users under the age of 18 on social media platforms, passed the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday. This bipartisan legislation would also ensure minors are aware of the potential mental health risks posed by social media usage and are provided access to mental health resources. | | | | | | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. subject: It's Friday, time to tax billionaires yet?

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=2032%2E251025%2E2TFWng ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=2032%2E251025%2E2TFWng ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

When we talk about providing guaranteed healthcare for everyone in America
or supporting small businesses, there’s one question that always comes up:
how are you going to pay for that?

The answers are simple: one, stop spending money on wars to bomb other
people’s children. And two, tax billionaire wealth!

So here's what we're going to do. We're going to build a tax system that’s
fair for working people and makes billionaires pay their fair share.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1213?t=1004&akid=2032%2E251025%2E2TFWng ]Your calculator app can’t tell the full story. So we built our own so
you can see exactly what this looks like.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1213?t=1005&akid=2032%2E251025%2E2TFWng ]GIF: Abdul saying: See at a billionaire tax of just 4% we could fund
ACA and medicaid subsidies that this guy [Trump] cut

If you tax a billionaire their fair share, you know what they are? Still a
billionaire.

Their kids, kids, kids, kids are still going to be rich. Maybe they could
pay their fair share so us and our kids don’t have to choose between one
part of a dignified life or another. It’s not that hard.

For example, at a billionaire tax of just 4%, we could fund ACA and
Medicaid subsidies that Republicans cut. We could fund vision, dental and
hearing for all of our seniors. We could cut payroll taxes, and we'd still
have money left over.

The fact that life has become so hard for so many is not a personal
failing. It's a policy failure of a government that has failed us for far
too long in a country where we're supposed to have a government of the
people, by the people, and for the people.

Friends, we can have that. Check out our billionaire wealth tax calculator
if you want to know for yourself what it's like to tax billionaires their
fair share.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1213?t=1006&akid=2032%2E251025%2E2TFWng ]BILLIONAIRE TAX CALCULATOR

— Team Abdul

Derek — I need you to look at this: [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-peltola-split?refcode=em_20260417_6747_fr&amount=20&refcode2=6747_22930333_Ktec_T&akid=6747%2E22930333%2EKtec_T) [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-peltola-split?refcode=em_20260417_6747_fr&amount=20&refcode2=6747_22930333_Ktec_T&akid=6747%2E22930333%2EKtec_T) The fight for fish, family, freedom is clearly a fight worth having. Alaskans want someone who will put Alaska first — and I will always do that. [**If you’re ready to flip Alaska and win nationwide, I am humbly asking you to split a donation between the DNC and my campaign for U.S. Senate today.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-peltola-split?refcode=em_20260417_6747_fr&amount=20&refcode2=6747_22930333_Ktec_T&akid=6747%2E22930333%2EKtec_T) **[SPLIT A $20 CONTRIBUTION](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-peltola-split?refcode=em_20260417_6747_fr&amount=20&refcode2=6747_22930333_Ktec_T&akid=6747%2E22930333%2EKtec_T)** Here’s the truth, Derek: Timing is everything, especially in a close race like this. Everyone is watching to see if we have the resources we’ll need to turn these polls into power — especially in a state as difficult to campaign in as Alaska. And when my opponent and his dark money backers see these polls and realize that we have what it takes to win this Senate seat and take on the rigged DC system, they’re going to spend big to try and stop us. That’s why we need a huge number of donations today to show everyone watching that we can and will win this fight for our future.
